result.title: DisFace3DNet: Explainable Facial Attractiveness Prediction via 3D Component Disentanglement
result.summary: Facial attractiveness prediction usually assigns one overall rating, leaving the roles of shape, appearance, and viewing conditions implicit. We propose DisFace3DNet, which uses 3D component disentanglement to learn seven component reference scores from overall ratings with auxiliary weak semantic supervision, without human-labeled component targets. Designated 3D representations and image cues feed jointly learned routes for identity, skin, hair, light, background, expression, and pose. A constrained fit then combines five static and two signed dynamic scores into the overall rating, exposing each component's numerical contribution and supporting component-specific comparisons across images. On SCUT-FBP5500, DisFace3DNet achieves a Pearson correlation of $0.8904\pm0.0063$ (mean $\pm$ standard deviation across five folds) with average human ratings; its component terms reconstruct every held-out prediction to numerical precision. Skin, hair, and facial shape account for the largest component-wise prediction variation. Human evaluation supports the score directions for facial shape, skin, and hair; expression agreement is weaker. DisFace3DNet thus connects overall prediction to quantitative analysis of the facial and contextual cues entering each estimate.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 DisFace3DNet，用 3D 部件解耦在仅有整体评分和弱语义监督下学习七个面部/情境部件的参考分，再经约束拟合组合为总评分，在 SCUT-FBP5500 上取得 0.8904 的人评相关，并给出各部件的数值贡献。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作把整体预测拆解为可解释的部件贡献、且在无部件级标注下学习，可能为 LVR 中答案对 latent 推理成分的贡献分配与弱监督提供可供核查的类比线索。
